assessmentSummary.identity: Pike Fold-to-Tall Sit is one seated bodyweight cycle: begin tall with both legs extended together on a stable floor or mat, fold forward from the hips toward the shins only through a comfortable controllable range, then return to a tall stacked seated position before the next repetition. It is not a static pike stretch, a bent-knee fold, a straddle fold, a sit-up, a loaded mobility drill, a V-up, or an assessment.
currentCardFindings: Source 73 states the broad seated fold-to-tall contrast but leaves exact start/finish, range, count unit, dose, surface, fatigue, stop rules, relationships, evidence, and media review unspecified.

The seated base, extended-together legs, repeated forward-fold-to-tall return, and no forced end-range rule form one coherent exact candidate. Changing knee position, leg separation, support, external load, static versus repeated action, or terminal posture changes the task or its delivery contract.

Three direct YouTube search results are stored only as unverified non-embedded candidates. Search-result visibility is not playback, exact-cycle, safety, accessibility, quality, or approval verification.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Sit tall on a clean stable mat or floor with both legs extended together. Fold forward from the hips toward the shins through a comfortable controllable range, then return to a tall stacked seated position before the next repetition. One complete fold-and-tall-return is one repetition. Pause and reset between repetitions. Range, reach target, breath, tempo, repetitions, rest, surface, and cueing are delivery annotations. Static pike stretches, bent-knee folds, straddle folds, sit-ups, V-ups, loaded work, assessments, and clinical interventions are different tasks requiring their own reviewed variant or definition.
